questions.q: A particle is travelling $4$ times as fast as an electron. Assuming the ratio of de-Broglie wavelength of a particle to that of electron is $2: 1,$& the mass of the particle is :-
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{p}$
$\dfrac{\lambdap}{\lambdae} = \dfrac{pe}{pp} = \dfrac{{m}_{e}{v}_{e}}{{m}_{p}{V}_{p}}$
$2 = \dfrac{me}{mp} \left(\dfrac{ve}{4{v}_{e}}\right)

questions.q: The threshold frequency of a metal with work function $6 . 63eV$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the work function of the metal is given by

${ϕ}_{0} = h{v}_{0} . . . \left(1\right)$

From equation (1), it follows that

$6 . 63 \times1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19} =6 . 63 \times {10}^{- 34}{v}_{0}⇒ {v}_{0} = $\dfrac{1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}}{10- 34}$⇒ {v}_{0} = 1 . 6 \times {10}^{15}Hz

$

questions.q: The work functions of Aluminium and Gold are $4 . 1eV$ and $5 . 1eV$ respectively. The ratio of the slope of the stopping potential versus frequency plot for Gold to that of Aluminium is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The data given is&

${ϕ}_{Al} = 4 . 1eV$

${ϕ}_{Au} = 5 . 1eV$

The energy is given by~

$hν = ϕ + KE ⇒ hν = ϕ + e{V}_{0}$

where~${V}_{0}$~is the stopping potential and~$K = e{V}_{0}$

Thus, the above equation can be written as

$e{V}_{0} = hν - ϕ$

$⇒ {V}_{0} = \dfrac{hν}{e} - \dfrac{ϕ}{e}$

The equation is of the form of~$y = mx + c$. The slope is~

$m = \dfrac{h}{e}$.

Since the Planck constant~$h$~and charge of an electron is a constant~$e$, the slope does not depend on the work function. Hence the ratio of the slope of the plot of stopping potential and frequency for both the given metals is~$1$.

questions.q: The kinetic energy of emitted electron is $E$ when the light incident on the metal has wavelength $\lambda$. To double the kinetic energy, the incident light must have wavelength:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using Einstein's photoelectric equation, kinetic energy of an electron is& $E$~when the incident wavelength is~$\lambda$~is~$E = \dfrac{hc}{λ} - ϕ . . . \left(1\right)$

When kinetic energy doubles, then,~$2E = $\dfrac{hc}{\lambda '} -$ϕ . . . \left(2\right)$

Subtracting~ \left($2\right) - \left(1\right)$, we have~

$E = hc \left(\dfrac{1}{\lambda '} - \dfrac{1}{λ}\right)

$⇒ {λ}^{'} = \dfrac{hc\lambda}{E\lambda + hc}$

$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion $\mathbf{A}$ and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A: Number of photons increases with increase in frequency of light.
Reason R: Maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons increases with the frequency of incident radiation.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{R}$ are correct and $\mathbf{R}$ is the correct explanation of $\mathbf{A}$.
Both $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{R}$ are correct and $\mathbf{R}$ is NOT the correct explanation of $\mathbf{A}$.
$\mathbf{A}$ is not correct but $\mathbf{R}$ is correct.
$\mathbf{A}$ is correct but $\mathbf{R}$ is not correct.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Intensity of light $\mathrm{I}=\frac{\mathrm{nh} \nu}{\mathrm{A}}$ Here $\mathrm{n}$ is no. of photons per unit time. $\mathrm{n}=\frac{\mathrm{IA}}{\mathrm{h} \nu}$ so on increasing frequency $v, \mathrm{n}$ decreases taking intensity constant. $\mathrm{k}_{\max }=\mathrm{h} v-\phi$
So on increasing $v$, kinetic energy increases.

questions.q:
The ratio of the de-Broglie wavelengths of proton and electron having same kinetic energy:
(Assume ${m}_{p} = {m}_{e} \times 1849$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The de-Broglie wavelength is given by&

$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{p} = \dfrac{h}{2mK} ( \text{As}, p^{2} = 2mK )$.

It is given that

~$( K{)}_{e} = ( K{)}_{p}$

Thus, the ratio of the wavelengths of the proton and electron is~
~ ~ ~ ~
~ & $\dfrac{\lambdap}{\lambdae} = \dfrac{2K{m}_{e}}{2K{m}_{p}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{me}{mp}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{1849}} = \dfrac{1}{43}$.

questions.q:
A monochromatic light is incident on a metallic plate having work function $\phi$. An electron, emitted normally to the plate from a point $A$ with maximum kinetic energy, enters a constant magnetic field, perpendicular to the initial velocity of electron. The electron passes through a curve and hits back the plate at a point $B$. The distance between A and B is :
(Given : The magnitude of charge of an electron is e and mass is $\mathrm{m}, \mathrm{h}$ is Planck's constant and c is velocity of light. Take the magnetic field exists throughout the path of electron)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{KE}_{\max }=\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda}-\phi \\ & \mathrm{p}=\sqrt{2 \mathrm{mK}_{\max }} \\ & \mathrm{p}=\sqrt{2 \mathrm{~m}\left(\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda}-\phi\right)} \\ & \mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B}}=2 \mathrm{R} \\ & =2\left[\frac{\mathrm{p}}{\mathrm{qB}}\right]\end{aligned}$
$\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{AB}}=\frac{2 \sqrt{2 \mathrm{~m}\left(\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda}-\phi\right)}}{\mathrm{eB}}=\frac{\sqrt{8 \mathrm{~m}\left(\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda}-\phi\right)}}{\mathrm{eB}}$

questions.q: The de-Broglie wavelength of a particle having kinetic energy $E$ is $\lambda .$ How much extra energy must be given to this particle so that the de-Broglie wavelength reduces to $75 %$& of the initial value?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Recall the formula of de-Broglie wavelength,& $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{p}$, here~$p$~is the linear momentum of the particle, now use the relation between linear momentum and kinetic energy,~$p = \sqrt{2Em} ⇒ E ∝ \dfrac{1}{\lambda2}⇒ E = \dfrac{k}{\lambda2}$

$\text{and}E^{'} = \dfrac{16k}{9{λ}^{2}} ⇒ \Delta E = \dfrac{7E}{9}$.

questions.q:
In a photoelectric experiment, ultraviolet light of wavelength $280$ nm is used with lithium cathode having work function $ϕ = 2 . 5eV$. If the wavelength of incident light is switched to $400$ nm, find out the change in the stopping potential.

\left(h = 6 . 63 \times {10}^{- 34}Js, c = 3 \times {10}^{8}\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}\right)$

$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From the photoelectric equation,

$e{V}_{0} = \dfrac{hc}{λ} - ϕ$

Using this equation for the given two cases,

$e{V}_{1} = \dfrac{hc}{280nm} - ϕ$

$e{V}_{2} = \dfrac{hc}{400nm} - ϕ$

On subtracting,

$e\left({V}_{1} - {V}_{2}\right) = 1240\left(\dfrac{120}{280 \times 400}\right) = 1.3eV$

$⇒ \left({V}_{1} - {V}_{2}\right) = 1 . 3V$

questions.q: An $\alpha$& particle, a proton and an electron have the same kinetic energy. Which one of the following is correct in case of their de-Broglie wavelength:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know, de-Broglie wavelength is given by,

$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{p}$

and~$p = \sqrt{2mK}$

Therefore,

$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{2mK}$

As kinetic energy is the same for all particles,

$∴ \lambda ∝ \dfrac{1}{m}$

$∵ {m}_{α} > {m}_{p} > {m}_{e}$

${λ}_{e} > {λ}_{p} > {λ}_{α}$

questions.q: The ratio of de-Broglie wavelength of an $\alpha$-particle and a proton accelerated from rest by the same potential is $\dfrac{1}{m}$ , the value of $m$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know, de Broglie wavelength in terms of energy of particle is given by,& $\lambda = \dfrac{1}{2mE}$.

Energy gained by proton,~$E = qV$.

Therefore,

$\dfrac{\lambda\alpha}{\lambdap} = \dfrac{\dfrac{h}{2{m}_{α}{q}_{α}V}}{h\sqrt{2{m}_{p}{q}_{p}V}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\lambda\alpha}{\lambdap} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{8}}$

$⇒ m = 8$

questions.q: In photoelectric experiment energy of $2.48 \mathrm{eV}$ irradiates a photo sensitive material. The stopping potential was measured to be $0.5 \mathrm{~V}$. Work function of the photo sensitive material is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{eV} \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{s}}=\mathrm{h} \nu-\phi \\ & 0.5 \mathrm{~V}=2.48-\phi \\ & \text { work function }(\phi)=2.48 \mathrm{~V}-0.5 \mathrm{~V}=1.98 \mathrm{~V}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: An electron moving with speed $v$ and a photon moving with speed $c$, have the same D-Broglie wavelength. The ratio of the kinetic energy of the electron to that of a photon is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${λ}_{e} = {λ}_{Ph}$

$\dfrac{h}{pe} = \dfrac{h}{pph}$

$\sqrt{2m{k}_{e}} = \dfrac{Eph}{c}$

$2m{k}_{e} = \dfrac{ \left({E}_{ph}\right)2}${c2}$

$\dfrac{ke}{Eph} = \dfrac{Eph}{c2} $\left(\dfrac{1}{2m})

=\dfrac{pph}{c} \left(\dfrac{1}{2m}\right)

=\dfrac{pe}{c} \left(\dfrac{1}{2m}\right)$

$= \dfrac{mv}{c}\dfrac{1}{2m}$

$= \dfrac{v}{2c}$

$$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Emission of electrons in photoelectric effect can be suppressed by applying a sufficiently negative electron potential to the photoemissive substance.
Reason (R) : A negative electric potential, which stops the emission of electrons from the surface of a photoemissive substance, varies linearly with frequency of incident radiation.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both ((\mathbf{A})) and ((\mathbf{R})) are true and ((\mathbf{R})) is the correct explanation of ((\mathbf{A}))
Both ((\mathbf{A})) and ((\mathbf{R})) are true but ((\mathbf{R})) is not the correct explanation of ((\mathbf{A}))
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Assertion (A) is true because a sufficiently negative potential can repel and stop the emitted electrons from leaving the surface. Reason (R) is also true because the stopping potential (V_{\text {stop }}) varies linearly with the frequency (\nu) of the incident light (  \left($V_{\text {stop }}=$\frac{h}{e} \nu-\frac{\phi}{e}\right)$). However, (R) does not directly explain why a negative potential suppresses electron emission; it only shows how much potential is needed for different frequencies. Therefore, both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).$

questions.q:
From the photoelectric effect experiment, following observations are made. Identify which of these are correct
A. The stopping potential depends only on the work function of the metal.
B. The saturation current increases as the intensity of incident light increases.
C. The maximum kinetic energy of a photo electron depends on the intensity of the incident light.
D. Photoelectric effect can be explained using wave theory of light.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
(A) Stopping potential depends on both frequency of light and work function.
(B) Saturation current $∝$ intensity of light.
(C) Maximum KE depends on frequency.
(D) Photoelectric effect is explained using particle theory. In this phenomenon, when electromagnetic radiation (such as light) hits the material, the emission of electrons takes place. In the photoelectric effect, if the frequency is too low, no electron is seen getting freed. But, if the frequency is high enough, some electrons can be observed. These observations prove that the Light is made of particles. The energy of the particle increases with the frequency.

questions.q: The de Broglie wavelength of a molecule in a gas at room temperature  \left(300K\right)$ is ${λ}_{1}$. If the temperature of the gas is increased to $600K$, then the de Broglie wavelength of the same gas molecule becomes$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The root mean squared velocity of a gas is given by&

$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$

$⇒ v ∝ \sqrt{T}$

Let

~${T}_{1} = 300K{T}_{2} = 600K$

Taking velocity ratios at the given temperatures,

$\dfrac{v1}{v2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{T1}{T2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{300}{600}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{2}}$

The de Broglie wavelength is given by~$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{mv}$. So,

$\lambda ∝ \dfrac{1}{v}$

The ratio of the wavelengths is~

$\dfrac{\lambda1}{\lambda2} = $\left(\dfrac{v2}{v1}) = \dfrac{2}{1}$

$⇒ {λ}_{2} = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}{λ}_{1}\right)

questions.q: When radiation of wavelength $\lambda$ is incident on a metallic surface, the stopping potential of ejected photoelectrons is $4 . 8V$. If the same surface is illuminated by radiation of double the previous wavelength, then the stopping potential becomes $1 . 6V$. The threshold wavelength of the metal is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${V}_{S} = hv - ϕ$

$4 . 8 = \dfrac{hc}{λ} - ϕ . . . ( i )$

$1 . 6 = \dfrac{hc}{2\lambda} - ϕ . . . ( ii )$

Using above equation $( i )- ( ii )$

$3 . 2 = \dfrac{hc}{λ} - \dfrac{hc}{2\lambda}$

$3 . 2 = \dfrac{hc}{2\lambda} . . . ( iii )$~

\left[\lambda = \dfrac{hc}{6 . 4}\right]$

Put in equation $( ii )$

$ϕ = 1 . 6$

$\dfrac{hc}{\lambdath} = 1 . 6$

${λ}_{th} = \dfrac{hc}{1 . 6}$

$= \left(\dfrac{hc}{6 . 4}\right) \times 4 = 4\lambda$

$

questions.q: An electron and proton are separated by a large distance. The electron starts approaching the proton with energy $3$ eV. The proton captures the electrons and forms a hydrogen atom in second excited state. The resulting photon is incident on a photosensitive metal of threshold wavelength $4000A$ What is the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectron?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Initially, energy of electron $= + 3eV$

finally, in ${2}^{nd}$ excited state,

energy of electron $= - \dfrac{( 13 . 6eV )}{32}$

$= - 1 . 51eV$

Loss in energy is emitted as photon,

So, photon energy $\dfrac{hc}{λ} = 4 . 51eV$

Now, photoelectric effect equation

${KE}_\max = \dfrac{hc}{λ} - ϕ = 4 . 51 - \left(\dfrac{hc}{\lambdath}\right)

$= 4 . 51eV - $\dfrac{12400eVA}{4000A}

$= 1 . 41eV$

$
